title: Rigidity
statement:
Let $X$ be a proper geometrically integral $k$-scheme, let $Y$ be a
$k$-scheme of finite type, let $Z$ be a $k$-scheme, and let
$h:X\times Y\to Z$ be a morphism. If $h$ maps $X\times y_0$ to a single
point for some $y_0\in Y$, then there are an open neighbourhood $V$ of
$y_0$ and a morphism $g:V\to Z$ with $h=g\circ\operatorname{pr}_2$ on
$X\times V$.

proof.text:
Let $W\subset Z$ be an affine open containing $h(X\times y_0)$. Since
$X$ is proper, the image in $Y$ of the closed set $h^{-1}(Z\setminus W)$
is closed, and its complement contains $y_0$; let $V$ be an affine
open neighbourhood of $y_0$ in this complement. Then $h$ maps
$X\times V$ into the affine scheme $W$, so it is determined by the ring
map $\mathcal O(W)\to H^0(X\times V,\mathcal O)$ (Stacks [01I1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01I1)). By flat
base change (Stacks [02KH](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02KH)) and $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ (Stacks [0BUG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BUG)), we
have $H^0(X\times V,\mathcal O)=\mathcal O(V)$. Hence the ring map is
$\operatorname{pr}_2^*$ composed with a ring map $\mathcal O(W)\to\mathcal O(V)$,
which defines $g$.
